note: Review-only companion; not a TestsData row. Answer rationales included; full editorial and distractor-specific review should precede production insertion.

questions.text: In the sentence “The technician repaired the computer,” which word is the verb?
questions.rationale: Repaired expresses the action.

questions.text: Which word is an adjective in “The careful student checked the result”?
questions.rationale: Careful describes the noun student.

questions.text: Which word is a pronoun?
questions.rationale: They stands in place of a noun phrase.

questions.text: Which sentence is interrogative?

options.label: D
options.text: What time does the lab open?

questions.rationale: An interrogative sentence asks a question.

questions.text: Which sentence is imperative?
questions.rationale: An imperative expresses a command or request.

questions.text: Choose the correct simple-present form: “She ___ to college by bus.”
questions.rationale: Third-person singular takes goes in the simple present.

questions.text: Choose the correct past tense: “Yesterday, we ___ the museum.”
questions.rationale: Yesterday signals a completed past event.

questions.text: Which sentence has correct subject–verb agreement?

options.label: A
options.text: The list of items be ready.

options.label: B
options.text: The list of items are ready.

options.label: C
options.text: The list of items is ready.

options.label: D
options.text: The list of items were ready.

questions.rationale: The subject is singular list; the phrase of items does not change its number.

questions.text: Choose the suitable modal for ability: “When he was six, he ___ swim.”
questions.rationale: Could expresses past ability.

questions.text: Which is the passive form of “The clerk filed the report”?

options.label: A
options.text: The clerk was filed by the report.

options.label: B
options.text: The report was filed by the clerk.

options.label: C
options.text: The report has filing the clerk.

questions.rationale: Simple past passive uses was/were + past participle.

questions.text: Choose the correct article: “She is ___ honest employee.”
questions.rationale: Honest begins with a vowel sound, so an is used.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: “The meeting starts ___ 10 a.m.”
questions.rationale: At is used for a specific time.

questions.text: Which is a complete sentence?
questions.rationale: The third option contains a complete independent clause.

questions.text: Which sentence uses the present continuous correctly?
questions.rationale: Present continuous is formed with am/is/are + -ing.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: “Neither of the answers ___ correct.”
questions.rationale: Neither is treated as singular in this formal construction.

questions.text: Which modal expresses advice?
questions.rationale: Should commonly expresses advice.

questions.text: Change to passive: “The team prepares the slides.”

options.label: A
options.text: The slides were prepare by the team.

options.label: B
options.text: The slides are prepared by the team.

options.label: D
options.text: The team is prepared by the slides.

questions.rationale: Present simple passive uses are + prepared.

questions.text: Which punctuation correctly ends a direct question?
questions.rationale: A direct question normally ends with a question mark.

questions.text: Which word is an adverb in “The speaker explained the process clearly”?
questions.rationale: Clearly modifies how the speaker explained.

questions.text: Which sentence uses a conjunction to join two ideas?

options.label: C
options.text: The device is new but inexpensive.

questions.rationale: But joins two contrasting ideas.

questions.text: Which reading technique is used to locate a date in a long report quickly?
questions.rationale: Scanning searches for a specific detail such as a date.

questions.text: Which technique is most useful for getting the main idea of an article quickly?

options.label: A
options.text: Reading only the last word of each line

questions.rationale: Skimming gives a rapid overview of main ideas.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a topic sentence in a paragraph?

options.label: A
options.text: To state the paragraph's central idea

options.label: B
options.text: To provide only the final conclusion

questions.rationale: A topic sentence signals the paragraph's main point.

questions.text: Which source is usually best for a detailed definition of a technical term?

options.label: B
options.text: A relevant reference book or trusted technical source

questions.rationale: A relevant authoritative reference provides a more reliable definition.

questions.text: Which text type normally records the sequence, outcomes and relevant details of an event?
questions.rationale: An event report documents what happened and relevant outcomes.

questions.text: Which document is most appropriate to request official permission for leave from a college?

options.label: D
options.text: An informal chat full of abbreviations

questions.rationale: A formal application suits an official request.

questions.text: Which opening is most suitable for a formal email to a faculty member whose name is known?
questions.rationale: A respectful salutation suits formal communication.

questions.text: Which detail most helps a reader understand an email's purpose before opening it?
questions.rationale: A descriptive subject summarizes the message purpose.

questions.text: Which greeting is suitable when introducing yourself in a formal presentation?

options.label: C
options.text: “You all know me, so no introduction.”

options.label: D
options.text: “I have no idea why I am here.”

questions.rationale: A brief respectful introduction identifies the speaker.

questions.text: Which presentation behaviour usually supports audience understanding?

options.label: A
options.text: Speaking while facing the screen throughout

options.label: B
options.text: Reading every slide word for word

options.label: C
options.text: Turning away during every key point

options.label: D
options.text: Using clear speech and looking at the audience periodically

questions.rationale: Clear speech and audience engagement improve communication.

questions.text: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
questions.rationale: Let's is the contraction of let us.

questions.text: Choose the correct plural: “The ___ are in the laboratory.”
questions.rationale: Equipment is generally an uncountable noun; use equipment with a plural verb where meaning permits.

questions.text: Choose the correct comparative: “This explanation is ___ than the previous one.”
questions.rationale: Clearer is the standard comparative form.

questions.text: Choose the correct word: “Please ___ the report before sending it.”
questions.rationale: The base verb follows please in this request.

questions.text: Which sentence has the clearest pronoun reference?

options.label: A
options.text: Rina submitted the file after Rina checked the figures.

options.label: B
options.text: After speaking to Meera, she left.

options.label: C
options.text: When Rina met Meera, she was late.

options.label: D
options.text: The student told the teacher that they were wrong.

questions.rationale: Repeating Rina avoids uncertainty about who performed the action.

questions.text: Which phrase is most appropriate in a formal application?

options.label: C
options.text: I request leave for two days due to illness.

questions.rationale: It is respectful and states the request clearly.

questions.text: Which section usually contains the subject and purpose of a formal email?

options.label: C
options.text: A random line in the signature

questions.rationale: The subject and opening establish the purpose.

questions.text: What should a concise event report generally include?

options.label: B
options.text: Relevant date, venue, activities and outcomes

questions.rationale: A report records relevant facts and outcomes.

questions.text: Which is the best response when an audience member asks a question you do not know how to answer?

options.label: C
options.text: Acknowledge the question and offer to verify the information

questions.rationale: Acknowledging limits and checking the facts is credible.

questions.text: Which pronunciation practice is most useful for a technical presentation?

options.label: A
options.text: Practise key terms aloud and check unfamiliar pronunciations

options.label: D
options.text: Speak faster whenever a term is unfamiliar

questions.rationale: Rehearsal and checking unfamiliar terms support intelligibility.

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: “Each of the laboratory computers ___ a separate asset number.”
questions.rationale: Each is singular and takes has.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: “By the time the instructor arrived, the students ___ the setup.”
questions.rationale: Past perfect marks completion before another past event.

questions.text: Choose the correct modal: “You ___ save a backup before changing the system files.”
questions.rationale: Ought to expresses strong advice in this context.

questions.text: Choose the correct passive sentence for “The staff will publish the timetable tomorrow.”

options.label: C
options.text: The staff will be published the timetable.

options.label: D
options.text: The timetable will be published tomorrow.

questions.rationale: Future passive uses will be + past participle.

questions.text: Choose the correct reported form: He said, “I am ready.”

options.label: A
options.text: He said that I am ready.

options.label: B
options.text: He said that he was ready.

options.label: D
options.text: He says that he were ready.

questions.rationale: In standard backshift, am becomes was and I changes to he.

questions.text: Select the sentence with correct subject–verb agreement.

options.label: A
options.text: The quality of these components have high.

options.label: B
options.text: The quality of these components were high.

options.label: C
options.text: The quality of these components are high.

options.label: D
options.text: The quality of these components is high.

questions.rationale: The head noun quality is singular.

questions.text: Choose the correct relative pronoun: “The technician ___ repaired the monitor is here.”
questions.rationale: Who refers to a person acting as the subject.

questions.text: Choose the sentence that expresses a condition correctly.

options.label: A
options.text: If the file will save, we can closed it.

options.label: B
options.text: If saved the file, we can closing.

options.label: C
options.text: If the file is saved, we can close the program.

options.label: D
options.text: If the file saved, we can closes.

questions.rationale: The first conditional uses present simple in the if-clause and can/will in the result.

questions.text: Which sentence avoids a dangling modifier?

options.label: A
options.text: Walking into the lab, the bright lights were noticed.

options.label: B
options.text: The lights, walking into the lab, looked bright.

options.label: C
options.text: Walking into the lab, the lights looked bright.

options.label: D
options.text: Walking into the lab, I noticed the bright lights.

questions.rationale: The person walking is the subject of the main clause.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: “The list of participants, along with the instructor, ___ on the desk.”
questions.rationale: The head noun list is singular; along with does not make it plural.

questions.text: A passage says the lab stayed open until 6 p.m., although the posted schedule said 5 p.m. Which conclusion is directly supported?

options.label: A
options.text: The lab always closes at 6 p.m.

options.label: B
options.text: On that occasion, the lab stayed open one hour beyond the posted time.

options.label: D
options.text: The lab was closed all day.

questions.rationale: The text supports a specific event, not a permanent rule.

questions.text: A report states, “The number of visitors rose from 120 to 150.” What was the numerical increase?
questions.rationale: 150 − 120 = 30 visitors.

questions.text: An article presents a claim and then gives two examples. What is the best reading approach to evaluate whether the examples support the claim?

options.label: A
options.text: Assume every example proves the claim

options.label: C
options.text: Count the number of paragraphs only

options.label: D
options.text: Identify the claim and compare each example with it

questions.rationale: Evaluation requires comparing supporting details with the main claim.

questions.text: An email asks for a reply by 4 p.m. and includes three optional background links. Which detail should the recipient note first to act appropriately?
questions.rationale: The reply deadline is the action-critical detail.

questions.text: Which subject line best fits an email requesting approval for an industrial visit on 12 November?

options.label: B
options.text: Industrial visit, and also several unrelated matters

options.label: C
options.text: Request for Approval: Industrial Visit on 12 November

questions.rationale: The subject states the purpose and relevant date.

questions.text: Which sentence is most appropriate in a formal request email?

options.label: A
options.text: I'd be grateful if you could approve the attached plan by Friday.

options.label: D
options.text: You must do it because I said so.

questions.rationale: It uses a polite request and a specific deadline.

questions.text: An event report must distinguish facts from opinion. Which entry is a verifiable fact?

options.label: A
options.text: The event was the best in college history.

options.label: B
options.text: The seminar began at 10 a.m. and had 85 registered attendees.

questions.rationale: Time and attendance can be verified; the other statements are evaluative.

questions.text: A student must present three reasons supporting a recommendation. Which structure is clearest?

options.label: A
options.text: Put the conclusion first, omit reasons

options.label: B
options.text: Use a single paragraph of run-on sentences

options.label: D
options.text: State the recommendation, give three ordered reasons with evidence, then conclude

questions.rationale: A clear claim-reasons-evidence-conclusion structure improves coherence.

questions.text: A listener asks for clarification during a presentation. What is the most effective response?

options.label: A
options.text: Pause, restate the point in simpler words, and check whether it is clear

options.label: B
options.text: Tell the audience the question is irrelevant

options.label: C
options.text: Repeat the same sentence more loudly without checking understanding

options.label: D
options.text: Ignore the question until the end

questions.rationale: Clarifying and checking comprehension responds directly to the need.

questions.text: A presenter uses highly technical terms with a mixed audience. What is the strongest adjustment?

options.label: C
options.text: Define essential terms briefly and use examples at the audience's level

questions.rationale: Audience-appropriate explanation supports understanding.

questions.text: Choose the sentence in which the modal expresses obligation rather than possibility.

options.label: C
options.text: Users must log out before maintenance.

questions.rationale: Must expresses an obligation or requirement.

questions.text: Choose the correct verb form: “Neither the students nor the lab assistant ___ available.”
questions.rationale: With neither/nor, the verb usually agrees with the nearer subject; lab assistant is singular.

questions.text: Which revision corrects the passive voice error in “The instructions was printed yesterday”?

options.label: C
options.text: The instructions are printed yesterday by them.

questions.rationale: Plural instructions takes were + past participle.

questions.text: Select the sentence with correct parallel structure.

options.label: A
options.text: The role requires to plan, testing and documentation.

options.label: B
options.text: The role requires planning, testing and documenting results.

options.label: C
options.text: The role requires planning, to test and documentation results.

options.label: D
options.text: The role requires planning, testing and to document results.

questions.rationale: All list items are gerunds: planning, testing, documenting.

questions.text: A passage states that a new bus route cut a journey from 50 minutes to 35 minutes. What is the decrease in travel time?
questions.rationale: 50 − 35 = 15 minutes.

questions.text: A passage says “Some students prefer printed notes, while others revise using digital files.” Which inference is strongest?

options.label: B
options.text: Students may use different revision preferences.

options.label: D
options.text: Printed notes always produce better marks.

questions.rationale: The sentence establishes different preferences only.

questions.text: An application needs a clear purpose and the dates requested. Which opening is best?

options.label: B
options.text: You know why I am writing.

options.label: C
options.text: I request leave from 14 to 16 December because of a scheduled medical appointment.

options.label: D
options.text: This is about something I need.

questions.rationale: It states the request, dates and reason concisely.

questions.text: Which revision improves clarity: “Due to the fact that the device overheated, therefore we stopped the test”?

options.label: A
options.text: Because the device overheated, we stopped the test.

options.label: B
options.text: Because of the reason that the test stopped.

options.label: C
options.text: Due to the device overheating, therefore the test was stopped by us.

options.label: D
options.text: The device overheated, because therefore we stopped.

questions.rationale: The revision removes redundant connectors and keeps a clear cause-effect relationship.

questions.text: A speaker has only 90 seconds to explain a process with six steps. What should they do?

options.label: A
options.text: Read every detail at maximum speed

options.label: B
options.text: Group related steps, highlight key actions, and leave time for a brief summary

options.label: C
options.text: Skip the objective and repeat the title

options.label: D
options.text: Show a dense slide and remain silent

questions.rationale: Grouping and prioritizing allows the limited time to be used effectively.

questions.text: Which statement is the strongest closing for a recommendation presentation?

options.label: B
options.text: The topic is complicated, so no decision is possible.

options.label: C
options.text: That is all, and I do not know what to add.

options.label: D
options.text: To conclude, the trial met the stated criteria; I recommend a monitored rollout and review after one month.

questions.rationale: It summarizes evidence and states a specific next step.

questions.text: Which revision is most concise and formal?

options.label: A
options.text: The request review, it is taking place.

options.label: B
options.text: At this point in time, we are currently reviewing the request.

options.label: C
options.text: We are doing a review of the request at the present time now.

questions.rationale: The sentence removes redundant wording.

questions.text: A teammate writes an email to request missing attendance data. Which version is most actionable?

options.label: A
options.text: Please send the attendance totals for 1–10 October by 3 p.m. Thursday so I can finish the report.

questions.rationale: It specifies the data, period, deadline and purpose.

questions.text: An event report includes time, venue, agenda, attendance and outcomes, but omits the writer's unsupported claim that the event was 'perfect'. What is the main benefit?

options.label: B
options.text: It prioritizes verifiable reporting over subjective praise

options.label: C
options.text: It converts the report into an informal message

options.label: D
options.text: It makes the report impossible to read

questions.rationale: Objective detail supports a credible report.

questions.text: A presentation slide contains eight sentences in small type. What change most likely improves readability without losing the key message?

options.label: A
options.text: Add multiple animations to every sentence

options.label: C
options.text: Turn the content into a clear heading and a few concise points, then explain details orally

options.label: D
options.text: Remove the heading and shrink the type

questions.rationale: Concise key points reduce visual load and support the speaker's explanation.

questions.text: A presenter notices the audience looking confused after a technical definition. What is a useful immediate response?

options.label: A
options.text: Give a short example or analogy and invite a clarification question

options.label: D
options.text: Repeat the definition word-for-word and move on

questions.rationale: An example can make an abstract definition more accessible.

questions.text: Which pair contains a common formal-email closing and a suitable use?

options.label: B
options.text: “Later!!!” — a report to a department head

options.label: C
options.text: “Yours sincerely” — a formal message to a named recipient

questions.rationale: Yours sincerely is appropriate in many formal letters to a named recipient.

questions.text: A report describes a student event held yesterday. Which tense is best for completed activities?
questions.rationale: Completed event activities are normally described in the past tense.

questions.text: Which note-taking method best helps prepare a short summary from a longer article?

options.label: B
options.text: Record the main claim and its most relevant supporting points

options.label: D
options.text: Record page numbers but no ideas

questions.rationale: A summary depends on the main idea and selected supporting details.

questions.text: The audience cannot hear the last row during a presentation. What should the speaker adjust first?

options.label: C
options.text: Project the voice clearly toward the audience and check audibility

options.label: D
options.text: Turn toward the screen and speak into it

questions.rationale: Clear projection toward the audience directly addresses audibility.

questions.text: During Q&A, a question has two parts. What response technique helps avoid missing one part?

options.label: A
options.text: Briefly restate the two parts, answer each in turn, and check if anything remains

questions.rationale: Separating and answering each part makes the response complete.

questions.text: Choose the sentence that correctly combines a past event completed before another past event.

options.label: A
options.text: When the supervisor arrived, we had already saved the file.

options.label: B
options.text: When the supervisor had arrived, we already save the file.

options.label: C
options.text: When the supervisor arrives, we had saved the file.

options.label: D
options.text: When the supervisor arriving, we have saved the file.

questions.rationale: Past perfect marks the earlier completed action; arrived marks the later event.

questions.text: Which revision correctly removes the unclear pronoun reference? Original: “Asha spoke to Nita after she completed the test.”

options.label: A
options.text: Asha and Nita spoke after she did it.

options.label: B
options.text: Asha spoke to Nita after Asha completed the test.

options.label: C
options.text: She spoke to her after completing the test.

options.label: D
options.text: After she completed the test, Asha spoke to Nita.

questions.rationale: Repeating Asha resolves who completed the test.

questions.text: A technician's instructions must describe four actions in the order performed. Which wording has the strongest procedural clarity?

options.label: B
options.text: Disconnect power and inspect things, then do the rest.

options.label: C
options.text: First disconnect power, then remove the cover, inspect the cable, and reconnect power only after refitting the cover.

options.label: D
options.text: Reconnect power before removing the cover, unless it is not needed.

questions.rationale: The sequence is explicit and preserves a safety-critical ordering.

questions.text: Choose the only grammatically correct sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: Each of the reports contain a summary.

options.label: C
options.text: Each of the report contain summary.

options.label: D
options.text: Each of the reports contains a summary.

questions.rationale: Each is singular and takes contains.

questions.text: A passage says an equipment upgrade reduced average processing time from 80 seconds to 60 seconds. What percentage reduction is reported?
questions.rationale: The reduction is 20/80 × 100 = 25%.

questions.text: A text states that the library expanded its hours in March after surveying users, but gives no attendance figures. Which statement is supported?

options.label: A
options.text: The library has always been open longer in March.

options.label: C
options.text: The survey proves every user supported the change.

options.label: D
options.text: The library expanded hours after a user survey.

questions.rationale: Only the action and timing are stated; outcomes are not given.

questions.text: A formal email asks for approval and must include an attachment, deadline and a respectful tone. Which draft is most complete?

options.label: A
options.text: Please approve the attached visit plan by Friday; let me know if any additional information is required.

options.label: D
options.text: I am sending something, so please decide.

questions.rationale: The first version states the action, identifies the attachment and sets a deadline politely.

questions.text: Which sentence preserves parallel construction in a project objective list?

options.label: A
options.text: The project aims at reducing delays, accuracy improved and errors.

options.label: B
options.text: The project aims to reduce delays, accuracy and to be fewer errors.

options.label: C
options.text: The project aims to reduce delays, improve accuracy and reduce errors.

options.label: D
options.text: The project aims to reduce delays, improving accuracy and fewer errors.

questions.rationale: Each objective uses the same verb structure.

questions.text: A presenter has evidence that a pilot worked with 12 participants. Which conclusion is best calibrated to the evidence?

options.label: A
options.text: The results are invalid because the group is not enormous.

options.label: B
options.text: The method will succeed for every department.

options.label: C
options.text: The pilot proves no further testing is useful.

options.label: D
options.text: The pilot suggests the method may help in similar settings, but a larger trial is needed.

questions.rationale: The conclusion acknowledges a promising result and the limitation of a small pilot.

questions.text: A reading question asks what cannot be concluded from a passage. Which approach is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Choose a statement that sounds familiar even if the passage is silent

options.label: B
options.text: Distinguish explicit facts and justified inferences from claims with no textual support

options.label: D
options.text: Assume a real-world fact must be mentioned in the passage

questions.rationale: A 'cannot conclude' question depends on the bounded text, not outside assumptions.

questions.text: Choose the best revision: “After reviewing the data, the conclusion was changed by the analyst because it was incomplete.”

options.label: A
options.text: The data was reviewing, so the conclusion changed it.

options.label: B
options.text: After reviewing the data, the analyst changed the conclusion because the earlier analysis was incomplete.

options.label: C
options.text: The analyst, after data, changed because incomplete.

options.label: D
options.text: After reviewing the data, the conclusion reviewed the analyst.

questions.rationale: The revision gives the reviewing action a clear subject and clarifies the reason.

questions.text: A report has evidence, a conclusion and a recommendation, but the conclusion repeats the opening word-for-word. What revision most improves its function?

options.label: C
options.text: Use the conclusion to synthesize the findings and lead logically to the recommendation

questions.rationale: A conclusion should synthesize rather than duplicate the opening.

questions.text: A passage says the company received 300 applications and interviewed 45 candidates. What proportion of applicants were interviewed?
A passage describes a trial at one campus and says the approach 'may be useful elsewhere'. Which interpretation respects the wording?

options.label: A
options.text: The text expresses a possibility, not a universal conclusion.

options.label: B
options.text: The trial happened at every campus.

options.label: C
options.text: The wording proves the approach failed.

options.label: D
options.text: The approach is proven effective at every campus.

questions.rationale: May signals cautious possibility rather than certainty.

questions.text: Which option best combines the two sentences without changing their meaning? “The server was unavailable. The team postponed the demo.”

options.label: A
options.text: The server was unavailable, the team and demo.

options.label: B
options.text: The server was unavailable, although the demo was postponed because it worked.

options.label: C
options.text: Because the server was unavailable, the team postponed the demo.

options.label: D
options.text: The team postponed the demo unless the server was unavailable.

questions.rationale: Because expresses the cause-effect relationship.

questions.text: A student must prepare a 3-minute presentation from a long technical report for non-specialists. Which workflow is most effective?

options.label: A
options.text: Identify one purpose, select essential findings, define key terms, use a simple visual and rehearse to time

options.label: B
options.text: Copy the abstract and read it aloud unchanged

options.label: D
options.text: Start from the final appendix and add no context

questions.rationale: Audience adaptation, prioritization and rehearsal are all needed.

questions.text: A formal application contains long background paragraphs but never states the requested action. What is the critical repair?

options.label: B
options.text: Add a clear request and relevant dates near the beginning

options.label: C
options.text: Move the request to a hidden footnote

questions.rationale: The recipient needs to identify the requested action immediately.

questions.text: An audience asks a challenging question that questions one slide's statistics. What should the presenter do first?

options.label: D
options.text: Acknowledge the concern, identify the figure/source and clarify what it does and does not show

questions.rationale: The presenter should address the evidence directly and candidly.

questions.text: A text contains a fact, an author's opinion and an inference. Which labeling method is sound?

options.label: A
options.text: Mark verifiable statements as facts, evaluative claims as opinions and reasoned but unstated conclusions as inferences

options.label: B
options.text: Treat all three as equally explicit facts

options.label: C
options.text: Label the longest statement as fact

options.label: D
options.text: Classify any sentence with a number as opinion

questions.rationale: These labels distinguish evidence from viewpoint and derived conclusion.

questions.text: A report must present events chronologically and explain the outcome. Which structure is clearest?

options.label: B
options.text: A list of adjectives followed by the title

options.label: C
options.text: Background/purpose, chronological activities, outcomes and concise conclusion

options.label: D
options.text: Outcome first, random anecdotes and no dates

questions.rationale: Chronological organization helps readers follow events and outcomes.

questions.text: A formal email asks a faculty member to review a project proposal and needs to mention an attached file. Which subject and opening are strongest?

options.label: A
options.text: Subject: Proposal; no greeting, no request, no deadline

options.label: B
options.text: Subject: Read this!!!; Hey, open it now.

options.label: C
options.text: Subject: Review Request — Project Proposal; Dear Professor, could you review the attached proposal by Thursday?

options.label: D
options.text: Subject: hi; I sent a thing.

questions.rationale: It identifies purpose, attachment, recipient and deadline.

questions.text: A report gives this data: attendance was 90, 105 and 120 over three successive sessions. Which statement is precise and avoids overclaiming?

options.label: A
options.text: Every future session will increase by 15.

options.label: D
options.text: Attendance increased by 15 at each successive session in the recorded data.

questions.rationale: The data shows two increments of 15, not a guaranteed future trend.

questions.text: An application requests leave from 8 to 10 January. Which detail is essential to make the request actionable?

options.label: A
options.text: A clear reason and dates, plus a request for approval

options.label: D
options.text: A long description of unrelated hobbies

questions.rationale: The recipient needs the period and relevant reason to assess the request.

questions.text: A slide says “The new process is faster” and lists times of 14 minutes before and 9 minutes after. Which rewrite best combines claim and evidence?

options.label: A
options.text: The process is the fastest in the world.

options.label: B
options.text: Recorded completion time fell from 14 to 9 minutes, a 5-minute reduction.

options.label: C
options.text: The process is faster because it is good.

options.label: D
options.text: The team always works faster now.

questions.rationale: The revised statement reports the measurable difference without exaggeration.

questions.text: The audience includes beginners and experienced technicians. How should the speaker handle essential technical vocabulary?

options.label: B
options.text: Avoid all technical terms even when needed

options.label: C
options.text: Use a different synonym every time

options.label: D
options.text: Define each important term briefly, then use the same term consistently

questions.rationale: Brief definitions and consistent terminology serve a mixed audience.

questions.text: A speaker loses their place after an audience question. Which preparation method best prevents the interruption from derailing the talk?

options.label: B
options.text: Use a clear outline with signposts and keep brief cue notes for the next section

options.label: C
options.text: End the session as soon as someone asks a question

options.label: D
options.text: Memorize every word and never use notes

questions.rationale: A structured outline and cues help resume the main line after interruptions.

questions.text: A student reports “Everyone agreed that the workshop was useful,” but only 4 of 20 respondents completed the feedback form. What is the best correction?

options.label: A
options.text: The response rate proves the event failed.

options.label: B
options.text: All participants found the workshop useful.

options.label: C
options.text: Four respondents submitted feedback; conclusions about all attendees cannot be drawn from those responses alone.

questions.rationale: A 20% response rate cannot represent all attendees without further evidence.

questions.text: An email contains a vague subject, an attachment with an unclear filename, and a deadline only in the final paragraph. Which revision most improves usability?

options.label: A
options.text: Use a specific subject, a descriptive filename and an early, explicit deadline

options.label: B
options.text: Make the email longer without changing organization

questions.rationale: Clear identification and prominent action details help the recipient act.

questions.text: A speaker is challenged about a statistic but is unsure of the source. What is the most credible response?

options.label: A
options.text: Insist the number must be right

options.label: B
options.text: State that you cannot verify the source immediately and offer to follow up with a checked reference

options.label: C
options.text: Ignore the question and change the slide

options.label: D
options.text: Invent a source on the spot

questions.rationale: Acknowledging uncertainty and committing to verified follow-up preserves credibility.

questions.text: A reading passage gives one example of a benefit but does not discuss cost. Which conclusion about cost is safest?

options.label: A
options.text: The benefit proves cost is irrelevant

options.label: D
options.text: The passage does not establish the cost

questions.rationale: A benefit example gives no evidence about cost.

questions.text: A presentation must recommend a network upgrade. Test data shows failures dropped from 12 to 3 in a pilot of 10 devices, but the sample is small. Which closing is best?

options.label: A
options.text: The upgrade eliminates all failures everywhere.

options.label: B
options.text: No decision can ever be made.

options.label: C
options.text: The data is irrelevant because ten devices were used.

options.label: D
options.text: The pilot showed fewer failures, so a larger controlled rollout is recommended before broad deployment.

questions.rationale: It uses the observed result but acknowledges the sample-size limit.

questions.text: A report draft includes an unsupported cause for a rise in attendance. The records show attendance rose, but no reasons were collected. What should the writer do?

options.label: A
options.text: Report the increase and note that the available data does not establish its cause

options.label: C
options.text: Claim that every participant gave the same reason

options.label: D
options.text: State the cause as fact because the rise is visible

questions.rationale: The data supports the trend, not an unmeasured cause.

questions.text: An email requests an urgent document, but the recipient's role is unclear and the deadline is unrealistic. What is the best communication strategy?

options.label: B
options.text: Clarify the required document, explain the reason for the deadline and propose a feasible time if needed

options.label: D
options.text: Copy every person in the organization immediately

questions.rationale: Clear purpose and a workable deadline help resolve ambiguity.

questions.text: During Q&A, two audience members ask conflicting questions about whether a trial is complete. The report says testing finished but monitoring continues. What is the accurate response?

options.label: A
options.text: The project is permanently finished in every respect.

options.label: C
options.text: The planned testing phase is complete, while post-test monitoring is still ongoing.

options.label: D
options.text: The report contains no distinction between testing and monitoring.

questions.rationale: The answer preserves the distinction stated in the report.

questions.text: A student has to summarize a four-page passage in 80 words and keep the main claim and two key findings. Which technique is most suitable?

options.label: A
options.text: Identify the thesis, select two findings, remove examples and repetition, then check the word count

options.label: B
options.text: Retain all minor details and reduce font size

options.label: C
options.text: Write a personal response instead of a summary

questions.rationale: A summary prioritizes the central idea and essential evidence.

questions.text: A recommendation is supported by three measurements, but one was collected under different conditions. How should it be presented?

options.label: A
options.text: Pick whichever number supports the preferred conclusion

options.label: B
options.text: Combine all measurements as directly comparable without qualification

options.label: C
options.text: Report the comparable measurements and explain the differing condition before using the third value

options.label: D
options.text: Delete the methods from the report

questions.rationale: Differences in conditions affect valid comparison and should be disclosed.

questions.text: A speaker notices that a translated technical term confuses the audience. Which response best supports comprehension and accuracy?

options.label: A
options.text: Repeat it louder in the same unfamiliar wording

options.label: B
options.text: Replace the term with an unrelated word

options.label: D
options.text: Give the accepted term, explain it in plain language and provide a relevant example

questions.rationale: Plain-language explanation and an example retain the concept while improving understanding.

questions.text: A formal report describes an event held on 4 September but uses present tense for most completed activities. What is the best editing principle?

options.label: B
options.text: Use consistent past tense for completed events while retaining present tense for current conclusions or general facts

options.label: C
options.text: Use a different tense in every paragraph

options.label: D
options.text: Change every verb to future tense

questions.rationale: Consistent tense clarifies when events occurred.

questions.text: A presenter wants to persuade an audience while remaining evidence-based. Which approach is strongest?

options.label: B
options.text: Use confident language instead of evidence

options.label: C
options.text: State a recommendation, show relevant evidence and limits, address a likely objection, then give a specific next step

questions.rationale: Evidence, caveats and a clear action form a credible argument.

questions.text: A text indicates that a college is considering a new timetable but has not approved it. Which statement is justified?

options.label: A
options.text: The college is considering the timetable, but approval is not yet established.

options.label: C
options.text: The timetable will definitely be used.

questions.rationale: Considering a proposal does not establish approval or rejection.
